title: Establishing a Rat Model of Knee Osteoarthritis Using Polyurethane Composite Wraps
author: Lian, Xiaowen

steps.title: Prepare animal cohorts
steps.instruction: Obtain male Sprague‑Dawley rats (SPF grade, 180–200 g, 6–7 weeks old) from the Standard Laboratory Animal Center of Fujian University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, house them at 24–26 °C with a 12 h light/12 h dark cycle, provide food and water ad libitum, and allow 7 days of acclimation; then randomize 20 rats into a control group (n = 10) and a model group (n = 10) using a computerized random number table; on the day of fixation shave the right hind limb of all rats and sterilize the skin with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Gather materials and equipment
steps.instruction: Collect the following: Urgo® Elastic Bandage (8 cm × 2.5 m, Shanghai, China, China Medical Device Filing No. 20161621); medical polymeric fixation bandage from Zhuhai Jianfan Biotechnology (medical device registration No. Yue Zhu Xie Bei 20150007); 304 stainless‑steel wire (conventional, 3.0 cm × 2.0 cm); non‑elastic bandage (2.5 cm × 2.0 cm); polyurethane‑based polymer composite bandage (3.5 cm × 5.0 cm); Bruker BioSpec 70/20 7 T MRI scanner (Bruker Biospin, Ettlingen, Germany) with 1H surface receive coil (RF SUC 300, 30 mm ID) and transmit coil (RF RES 300); PerkinElmer Quantum GX2 micro‑CT system; Safranin O–Fast Green Staining Kit (G1053, Seville Biotechnology, Wuhan, China); TUNEL apoptosis detection kit (G1507‑50T, Xavier Biotechnology, Wuhan, China); MSHOT ML31 instrument; and standard laboratory supplies (cotton sleeves, ethanol, 75 % medical ethanol, 4 % paraformaldehyde, 10 % EDTA pH 7.4, ethanol series, xylene, paraffin, microtome, FIJI software, GraphPad Prism v10.1.2).

steps.title: Immobilize knee joint with bandages
steps.instruction: Place each rat in left lateral decubitus, cover the head with a soft cotton sleeve, trim hair 3–4 cm around the right knee, disinfect skin with 75 % medical ethanol, keep the right hind limb fully extended (0°), then:

substeps.instruction: Wrap a non‑elastic bandage (2.5 cm × 2.0 cm) in a spiral from the proximal third of the femur to the ankle, securing soft tissues and joint capsule.

Heat the polyurethane‑based polymer composite bandage until pliable, insert a 304 stainless‑steel wire (3.0 cm × 2.0 cm) along its long axis, and wrap the bandage spirally over the non‑elastic layer while maintaining full knee extension.
Allow the composite bandage to cool and harden, thereby fixing the knee in full extension.
Maintain immobilization for 6 weeks, checking bandages daily and replacing any that become wet or loose.

steps.title: Assess joint function with Modified Lequesne MG scale
steps.instruction: Evaluate knee dysfunction at baseline (pre‑modeling) and at weeks 2, 4, and 6 using the rodent‑validated Modified Lequesne MG scale (0–11 points). Conduct assessments in a quiet, temperature‑controlled room after 30 min acclimation; two blinded observers score gait pattern, joint swelling, range of motion, and nociceptive response as described, and record the average score. A total score ≥ 3 at week 6 confirms successful model induction.

steps.title: Perform MRI scanning
steps.instruction: One day after immobilization, sedate rats with isoflurane (2–3 % in O₂), position them supine with the right knee fully extended in a custom fixation cradle, and monitor respiration and body temperature throughout the scan. Acquire images on a Bruker BioSpec 70/20 7 T scanner using a 1H surface receive coil (RF SUC 300) and transmit coil (RF RES 300) with parameters: TR = 940.31 ms, TE = 20.5 ms, flip angle = 90°, slice thickness = 0.5 mm, FOV = 50 × 50 mm, NEX = 8. Scan five rats per group; have two experienced radiologists independently evaluate the images.

steps.title: Perform micro‑CT scanning
steps.instruction: After a 24‑h recovery, re‑anesthetize rats with isoflurane (2–3 % in O₂) and scan the right knee using a PerkinElmer Quantum GX2 system (90 kV, 80 µA, 72 mm FOV). Reconstruct projection data to obtain high‑resolution 2‑D cross‑sections and 3‑D images; MRI and micro‑CT are performed on the same cohort.

steps.title: Process knee cartilage for histology
steps.instruction: Six weeks post‑immobilization, euthanize rats with intraperitoneal 3 % sodium pentobarbital (30 mg/kg) followed by cervical dislocation; excise the right knee, photograph the femoral condyle cartilage surface, remove adherent tissue, and fix specimens in 4 % paraformaldehyde at room temperature for 24 h. Decalcify in 10 % EDTA (pH 7.4) at 4 °C for 6 weeks, changing solution every 3 days. Dehydrate through graded ethanol, clear in xylene, embed in paraffin, and cut longitudinal sections 5 µm thick.

steps.title: Stain sections and grade OARSI score
steps.instruction: Stain paraffin‑embedded sections with Safranin O–Fast Green (Kit G1053) and evaluate cartilage damage using the modified OARSI grading system (0–6). Examine four standardized regions per section (anterior/posterior medial femoral condyle and anterior/posterior medial tibial plateau) at 40 × magnification, sum the scores of the four regions to obtain the total OARSI score for each specimen.

steps.title: Measure chondrocyte apoptosis
steps.instruction: Apply the TUNEL apoptosis detection kit (G1507‑50T) to the sections following the manufacturer’s protocol; identify TUNEL‑positive nuclei (brown‑yellow). For each group (n = 3 samples), randomly select five fields of view per sample, count total chondrocytes and TUNEL‑positive cells using FIJI software, and calculate apoptosis rate (%) = (TUNEL‑positive / total chondrocytes) × 100.

steps.title: Analyze data statistically
steps.instruction: Present data as mean ± standard deviation. Compare two independent groups with an unpaired t‑test (normal distribution) or Mann–Whitney U test (non‑normal). Use Mann–Whitney U for OARSI scores, unpaired t‑test for apoptosis rates, and one‑way ANOVA for Modified Lequesne MG scores across time points. Perform all analyses and graphing in GraphPad Prism v10.1.2; consider two‑tailed P < 0.05 as statistically significant.
